job.text: Is it true you'd rather be doing something other than {job}?
With {soldiers} soldiers on the rota, do you ever get drafted into the drills?
The caverns are open below us. Do you ever go down?

mood.text: The whole fort is waiting on the {moody_shop}. How are you holding up?
How has the fort been since {lastdead} died?
Has the rain reached your mood yet?

complaint.text: Too many cats, or not enough?
What do you make of the great thread mountain?
Is it the same old booze again?
How is the fort managing on so little food?

last.text: Anything you'd say to {enemy}, if they were reading?

mood_happy.text: Happy. I prayed, I ate at a table, I drank something new. A dwarf with nothing unmet is a dwarf who works well.
Happy. {artifact_new} is ours. I have seen it twice.

mood_ecstatic.text: Never better. I have friends, a god, a drink and a job I'm good at. That's all of the list.
Ecstatic. The fort made a legend this month and I was in the crowd.

mood_content.text: Content. Nothing wrong that a good meal and a new kind of drink wouldn't fix.
Content, though the rain is very loud on the surface even from down here. I am lying. I can't hear it at all.
Content. Waiting, like everyone, to see what comes out of the {moody_shop}.

mood_stressed.text: Stressed. I haven't prayed or talked to a friend in days, and I can feel the focus going.
Stressed. Since {lastdead} died I can't settle.
Stressed. We are at war with {enemy}, and nobody will tell me what that means for supper.

mood_very_stressed.text: Very bad. Haggard and drawn, the doctor says. I need a drink, a friend and a week off.
Terrible. The stores are almost empty and I can count my meals on one hand.

mood_breaking.text: Close to the edge. If I break something this week, I would like the record to show I warned you first.

deity.text: I pray to {deity}. A dwarf who needs to pray and can't is a dwarf who works badly.
I pray to {deity} at the temple, when the performers aren't using it.

signoff.text: Drink something different this week. It helps.
Bury your dead. Engrave a slab. Sleep well.
Bring the moody dwarf what they ask for.
Go and see {artifact_new} before the queue gets longer.
Don't feed the cats. They don't need it.

good.text: A new drink at last. I was getting tired of the same old booze.
Five mugs from one plump helmet, and I had two of them.

bad.text: The same wine again. And again. A dwarf needs variety.
Water. They gave me water. I'm not in the hospital.

good.text: A roast with three things I like in it. One meal, three favourites.
Cheese, fresh from the farmer's workshop. I'd vote for whoever made it.

bad.text: Raw plump helmet on the stairs again.
Quarry bush leaves, raw. Never again.

good.text: Prayed at the temple. My head is clearer than it's been all season.

bad.text: Haven't prayed in weeks. I can feel my focus slipping.

good.text: Saw a masterwork today. A good one makes the whole day better.
Stood in front of the artifact for an hour. Worth it.

bad.text: Someone broke a masterwork. Its maker hasn't spoken since.

good.text: A cat chose me. I didn't ask, but I'm honoured.
Watched the herd grazing moss in the pasture. Very peaceful.

bad.text: A pet died. The slab is small but I'll visit it.

good.text: A good spar at the barracks. On rota this month and glad of it.

bad.text: Saw a fight I couldn't stop. Still hear it.

good.text: Finally made something with my own hands. That itch is scratched.

bad.text: I need to make something, talk to someone, pray, anything. My focus is shot.
Haven't seen my family in a month. It's wearing me down.
Haven't talked to a friend in days. The tavern is right there and I keep walking past it.
Nothing exciting has happened in ages. I'd welcome a crundle.
Saw a body that hadn't been buried. That's how ghosts start.
Lost a friend. Grief doesn't haul itself away.
Walked through miasma on the way to work. Somebody forgot something rotten.

good.text: Getting better at my trade every day. One day, a masterwork.

bad.text: Slept on the floor. The barracks were full of the off-rota squad.

good.text: Saw the caravan come in. Wagons, animals, and somebody else's gossip.

decks.text: {dwarf}, {age}, the fort's {prof}, gave the Herald five minutes between jobs and spent four of them on the subject of drink variety.
We caught up with {dwarf}, {prof}, {age}, on the way to {job}, and asked what the fort is really talking about.
